parole.testo: From Italian pisello (“pea”), from Vulgar Latin *pisellum, diminutive of Latin pisum, from Ancient Greek πίσον (píson).

Several theories. According to Meyer a borrowing from Italian canto (canthus). According to Mann a cognate to Ancient Greek κανθός (kanthós, “corner of the eye”) - while seen as a loan from Ancient Greek κανθός (kanthós) by Topalli Orel claims it as an early borrowing from Proto-Slavic *kǫtъ.
